strengths: Novel motivation-grounded reasoning framework that principally decomposes ideation into motivation identification, reasoning trajectory, and methodology generation
Creative composite reward design synergizing entropy-aware information gain (EAIG) for technical depth with contrastive semantic gain (CSG) for logical direction
Comprehensive experimental analysis including thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-5) and training dynamics visualization that provide insights into component contributions
Rigorous theoretical analysis of length bias in GRPO and principled length anchoring solution (Appendix F)
Fair baseline comparisons with detailed adaptation protocols documented; strong alignment between human and LLM judge evaluations (r=0.715)
Reproducibility efforts including code release promise, detailed hyperparameters, implementation details, and data construction pipeline
weaknesses: Severely limited domain scope restricted to ML/CS (ICLR papers only); claims about general 'scientific ideation' are overstated given unvalidated transferability to other disciplines with different logical structures

Insufficient evaluation rigor: no statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; only 60 samples for human validation; subjective evaluation metrics (Novelty, Feasibility) acknowledged as inherently subjective

Synthetic reasoning chains via posterior reconstruction may not reflect actual scientific discovery processes; ground truth method sections are post-hoc descriptions rather than authentic discovery paths
Modest improvements over simpler SFT baseline (6.7%) raise questions about RL contribution beyond data diversity; unclear whether gains come from larger training corpus or principled RL optimization
Arbitrary design choices: entropy threshold (25%), CSG/EAIG weight ratios, embedding model for semantic similarity—insufficient justification or sensitivity analysis
Missing key comparisons: no oracle baseline using ground-truth motivations, no comparison to other scientific ideation methods (Sci-idea), no ablation on GRPO vs. simpler RL algorithms

Reproducibility concerns: unspecified computational requirements, dependence on specific base model and framework, RL training likely expensive, evaluation dataset comprises only ~2000 valid RL samples
No real-world validation; paper acknowledges feasibility cannot be measured without actual implementation. No systematic failure analysis or examples where baselines outperform MoRI

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear articulation of limitations in existing agentic approaches
Thoughtful dual-granularity reward framework (EAIG + CSG) with sound theoretical motivation and synergistic balancing
Rigorous experimental methodology including in-domain and OOD evaluation, human-LLM judge alignment validation (r=0.715), bootstrap confidence intervals, and Bonferroni-corrected significance testing
Comprehensive ablations (Tables 3-6, Figures 3-5) effectively isolating each component's contribution and demonstrating reward stability
Strong empirical results with consistent improvements in technical rigor (+2.9% vs Claude) and feasibility (+10.3%) across test sets
Extensive technical exposition enabling reproducibility through detailed appendices on implementation, baselines, evaluation protocols, and theoretical analysis
weaknesses: Severely limited scope: evaluation restricted to ML/NLP papers only (ICLR/NeurIPS); generalizability to biology, physics, or other scientific domains explicitly untested, making 'scientific ideation' claims overstated

Fundamental evaluation limitations: no practical validation that generated ideas are implementable or produce novel results; scoring relies on subjective LLM judgment (with systematic bias of +0.3-0.4 over human scores); OOD human-LLM correlations weaker (0.613-0.684, Table 13)

Synthetic reasoning trajectories (z) synthesized via posterior reconstruction lack validation; quality and fidelity of these LLM-rewritten chains are never assessed, raising questions about whether they represent actual scientific reasoning

Reward design contains ad-hoc elements: entropy threshold (top 25%) lacks principled justification; piecewise shaping parameters appear hand-tuned without sensitivity analysis; cosine similarity is crude for assessing novelty; EAIG-only shows severe collapse (Figure 3)

RL optimization concerns: length anchoring penalty appears to be post-hoc fix rather than addressing root causes; only GRPO tested; no comparison to alternative RL algorithms; soft reward signals vulnerable to small variance changes
Baseline comparison fairness issues: output expansion for AI-Scientist-V2, inconsistent backbone models, prompt design may not reflect intended baseline usage
Missing practical validation and error analysis; no evidence that high-scoring ideas are scientifically sound or implementable; minimal investigation of when/why MoRI fails
Train/test similarity: while split by paper, ICLR and NeurIPS papers are highly correlated in topics and methodology trends; true OOD testing requires different subfields
Limited insight into learned patterns: three reasoning behaviors identified anecdotally without quantitative analysis or statistical significance testing
Modest improvements over strong baseline: MoRI 3.18 vs Claude-3.5-Sonnet 3.11 (~2.3% relative improvement)

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem formulation of scientific ideation as motivation-driven reasoning
Comprehensive empirical evaluation with multiple baselines, LLM and human judges, statistical significance testing, and OOD validation
Rigorous ablation studies analyzing reward components, entropy masking, and training dynamics with clear visualizations
Honest limitations section acknowledging scope constraints and evaluation challenges
Methodologically sound experimental design with leakage prevention and stratified human validation
weaknesses: Core claim about 'learning scientific reasoning' is overclaimed and possibly circular: ground-truth motivations, methods, and reasoning trajectories are all LLM-extracted/synthesized, leading to pattern matching against training data rather than genuine reasoning

Evaluation does not validate actual scientific quality: LLM judges cannot assess true feasibility or novelty without real-world implementation; paper explicitly acknowledges feasibility 'cannot be fully measured without real-world experiments'

Modest empirical improvements: 8.5% over Full-SFT baseline and not statistically significant against Claude-3.5-Sonnet (p=n.s., overlapping CIs); AI-Scientist-V2 achieves competitive novelty scores (3.45 vs. 3.31)

Reward engineering appears brittle and heuristic-heavy: EAIG alone causes reward collapse and length explosion (Figure 3); requires piecewise step-function shaping, format constraints, and length anchoring penalties; CSG weights dominate (0.7 vs. 0.3), suggesting EAIG is mainly a destabilizer

Problematic reward design: EAIG uses entropy as proxy for 'hard knowledge' without validation that high-entropy tokens reflect technical importance; CSG incentivizes matching training data style rather than discovering novel insights

Data construction issues: synthetic reasoning trajectories reverse-engineered from ground truth via LLM backward inference may not reflect authentic reasoning; only ~8,000 samples (small by RL standards); no ablation validating necessity of z
Limited scope and generalization: tested only on CS/ML papers (ICLR/NeurIPS); transferability to other scientific domains explicitly acknowledged as untested; no cross-domain evaluation

Insufficient baseline comparisons: Full-SFT only scales data; AI-Scientist-V2 extensively adapted in Appendix D; no comparison of fine-tuned commercial models on same data, simpler RL objectives, or training without synthetic z

Reasoning quality never directly evaluated: only final methodology scores matter; unclear if generated reasoning actually influences outputs or is merely a memorized intermediate step; three identified 'reasoning patterns' (Appendix J) are post-hoc and unvalidated

Misleading framing: claims 'internalization of scientific reasoning' and 'motivation-grounded' when model is conditioned on ground-truth motivations; motivation-reasoning coupling is enforced architecturally, not learned; misapplies Bitter Lesson citation

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear distinction between surface-level pattern matching and internalized motivation-grounded reasoning

Novel composite reward framework combining entropy-aware information gain (targeting technical depth) with contrastive semantic gain (ensuring logical alignment), supported by theoretical analysis of length bias

Rigorous experimental methodology: temporal train/test split, OOD validation (NeurIPS), context-aware LLM judges with retrieved related works, human-LLM alignment (r=0.715, p<0.001), and appropriate statistical significance testing
Comprehensive ablation studies demonstrating contribution of each component; training dynamics analysis shows EAIG-only causes collapse while optimal mix prevents this
Strong empirical results across dimensions with robust OOD generalization (3.19 ICLR → 3.15 NeurIPS); meaningful improvements over baselines (+8.5% vs Full-SFT, +22% vs AI-Scientist-V2-GPT-4o)
Excellent reproducibility: detailed data pipeline with privacy controls, baseline adaptation guidelines, hyperparameter specifications, end-to-end example, and promised code release
Qualitative evidence of genuine learned reasoning: systematic reasoning traces (Figure 11) and identification of three distinct behavior patterns (Appendix J)
weaknesses: Severely limited domain scope: training and evaluation exclusively on ML/AI papers (ICLR 2024-2025, NeurIPS); no evidence of generalization to other scientific domains with different reasoning structures despite claims of 'authentic scientific discovery'

Evaluation validity concerns: subjective metrics remain despite human-LLM alignment; only 60 samples for correlation analysis; potential circular bias (trained on ICLR methods, evaluated against similar metrics); no real-world validation through peer review or adoption

Data construction issues: posterior reconstruction of reasoning trajectories z via LLM synthesis—no validation that reconstructed paths reflect actual scientific reasoning; de-symbolization loses technical precision crucial for distinguishing rigorous from superficial ideas

Incomplete reward design justification: entropy threshold (top 25%) appears ad-hoc with limited ablation (only compares 25% vs 50%); information gain restricted to high-entropy tokens could miss important novel technical content that's predictable in context

Modest improvements over strongest baseline: MoRI 3.18 vs Claude-3.5-Sonnet 3.11 (Δ=0.07, p=n.s., statistically insignificant); improvements concentrated in feasibility while Claude excels in novelty (complementary strengths, not clear superiority)

Incomplete failure mode analysis: no systematic study of ideas MoRI fails to generate; unclear whether unconventional or interdisciplinary ideas are systematically downscored; no aggregate error taxonomy

Baseline comparison limitations: AI-Scientist-V2 output expansion (200 words → full method) may introduce unfair length bias; no exploration of alternative prompting for commercial models; computational constraint substitutions (VirSci) weaken comparisons
Technical design underexplored: no justification for choosing GRPO over PPO/DPO; linear length penalty functional form not validated; sensitivity to embedding model choice for CSG not analyzed
